unresolved: Lines 24-25 index gage(:,2) and assign it into successive columns of en without checking that each loaded station file has a second column or the same row count; a short-column file causes an index error and unequal lengths cause an assignment-size mismatch.

Line 34 assumes at least 400 samples. If length(en)<400 the 400:length(en) index descends rather than representing an empty post-spinup interval, and subsequent statistics can select unintended rows or fail; no bound check is present.
Lines 44-52 divide third moments by standard deviations cubed without guarding zero or non-finite variance, so a constant/empty station series yields NaN or Inf and defeats the intended statistic.

Lines 77-81 divide RMSE by max(ske) or max(ae) without a zero/non-finite guard; because max is also a signed reference maximum rather than a magnitude scale, all-nonpositive reference data can produce a negative percentage.
The rmse calls at lines 77-81 rely on a function not defined in this file; compatibility depends on an external MATLAB/toolbox or path-provided implementation.

nhn is assigned at line 38 but never consumed, while nn is first a scalar sample count at line 36 and later deliberately overwritten as the 2:12 plotting/RMSE index at line 64; any later insertion expecting the sample count would silently receive an index vector.
content.what_it_is: MATLAB postprocessing script for the Mase-Kirby benchmark: it loads reference skewness/asymmetry (lines 9-12), loads 12 station time series and converts elevation to centimetres (lines 22-25), discards the first 399 samples (line 34), computes demeaned elevation skewness and Hilbert-transform asymmetry (lines 41-52), saves the derived arrays (line 54), compares them with another reference result in a plot (lines 57-74), and prints four normalized RMSE percentages (lines 77-81).
